info.title: motionEye
info.description:
The HTTP API of motionEye, the one its own web UI uses.

## Signing in

There are two users: the admin, who can change everything, and the normal (surveillance) user, who can watch and download.

Sign in with `POST /login/` and send back the `user` cookie it sets, as the web UI does. Sessions end when motionEye restarts. Requests without one are refused with `403` and `{"error": "unauthorized"}`.

## Conventions

Paths end with a slash. Changes are `POST`, with a JSON body. Many operations answer `200` with an `error` field when they fail, rather than with an error status. Live video comes from motion's own streaming port, not from this API.

servers.description: This motionEye server, including any base path it is served under.

200.description: The user of the session, or an error when there is none.
Signed in; the `user` cookie set by this response carries the session. Or an error, for wrong credentials.

force_password_change.description: True while the admin still has no password; the web UI then asks for one.

429.description: Too many failed sign-ins from this address; wait for the number of seconds in `Retry-After`.

post.description: Starts a session for the web UI or for a script that keeps cookies. Sessions are kept in memory, so they end when motionEye restarts. Repeated failures from one address are slowed down.

remember.description: Whether the cookie outlasts the browser. False gives a cookie the browser drops when it closes; the session ends on the server at the same time either way.

200.description: The session has ended and its cookie is cleared.

get.description:
Lists the cameras with their settings, as `/config/{camera_id}/get/` returns them. The normal user is not shown admin-only cameras, nor secrets such as passwords.

With `proto`, it instead lists the cameras that can be added from a source, which only the admin may do.

Open to both users.

post.summary: Run an action on a camera

200.description: Done, or an `error` saying why not. Custom actions report the exit status of their command.

status.description: For custom actions: the exit status of the command.

error.description: For the built-in actions: why it failed, or null.

400.description: The camera has no such action, or doesn't save snapshots.

post.description:
Built-in actions:

- `snapshot`: save a picture now. Refused when the camera doesn't save snapshots.
- `eventstart` and `eventend`: start or end a motion event as if motion had been detected.
- `detectionpause` and `detectionstart`: pause or resume motion detection, as the camera's detection button does, for example to disarm and arm an alarm. It changes the running motion and isn't saved: a working schedule takes over again at its next change, and motion's own settings at its next restart.

Any other name runs the camera's custom action script of that name, if it has one, such as `lock`, `unlock`, `light_on`, `alarm_on`, `up` or `preset1`.

Open to both users. The normal user cannot act on admin-only cameras.
